We additionally evaluate our model over 13,200 Monte Carlo games against 11 synthetic opponent archetypes, an ablation of the opponent-modeling layer, and an extensive analysis of 9,337 live-game messages in which moral rhetoric framing in the persuasion setting is strongly correlated with whether the buyer purchased ($χ^2=616.7$, $p \approx 3.7\times10^{-132}$), surviving controls for quality, round, and configuration.
items.title_ko: GLEE를 위한 베이즈 상대 모델링 및 도덕적 수사적 프레임을 갖춘 게임 이론 솔버
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 GLEE 대회에 제출된 에이전트를 설명하며, 이 에이전트는 인간 및 AI 상대방과의 협상 게임을 플레이합니다. 이 에이전트는 고전적 게임 이론 솔버, 상대 유형을 추정하는 온라인 베이즈 레이어, 그리고 메시지를 작성하는 언어 모델이라는 세 가지 핵심 구성 요소를 중심으로 구축되었습니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 협상 및 설득 게임에서 AI 에이전트의 전략적 의사결정 능력과 인간과의 상호작용 능력을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
items.body: Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion. In real-world deployment, however, desired execution behaviors are also defined by quality attributes such as execution speed and motion smoothness, which need to be dynamically controlled according to task requirements. To address this, we introduce Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), a robot policy that enables inference-time control over both individual quality attributes and their combinations. To extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations, we further propose an iterative hindsight relabeling loop: QCP collects online rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories to the dataset, relabels the accumulated trajectories in hindsight according to their measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy. Experiments on Robomimic and RoboEval demonstrate that QCP consistently improves both task execution quality and success rates across iterations, producing successful rollouts that exceed the quality of the initial demonstrations. Finally, we validate QCP on real-world manipulation tasks, where controlling speed increases throughput in conveyor operations and controlling transport stability improves success when carrying wine glasses, demonstrating that quality-controllable policies yield practical gains in physical deployment.
items.title_ko: 반복적인 사후 재라벨링을 통한 품질 제어 가능한 로봇 정책 학습
items.summary_ko: 로봇 정책 평가는 종종 작업 완료에 대한 이진 성공 신호에 의존하지만, 실제 배포에서는 실행 속도, 동작 부드러움과 같은 품질 속성도 중요합니다. QCP(Quality-Controllable Policy)는 개별 품질 속성과 그 조합 모두에 대한 추론 시점 제어를 가능하게 하는 로봇 정책을 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 단순히 작업을 성공하는 것을 넘어, 원하는 품질 수준으로 작업을 수행할 수 있도록 하여 로봇의 실제 환경 적용성을 크게 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction
items.body: Accurate acquisition of full channel state information (CSI) is essential for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) wireless systems, while dense pilot-based estimation incurs substantial overhead. Directly minimizing the prediction error over raw CSI coefficients is fragile in realistic propagation environments, since small-scale fading, mobility, local scattering, and small spatial perturbations can induce large phase-sensitive variations. Nevertheless, wireless channels contain strong spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain correlations that can be more predictably represented in a latent propagation-field domain. Motivated by this observation, we propose a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA)-inspired field world model, defined as a latent predictive model of the wireless propagation field, for sparse-pilot channel reconstruction. The model maps CSI observations into latent time-frequency tokens, predicts masked or future latent field states from historical multi-band context, and fuses the predicted latent prior with sparse noisy current pilots to reconstruct the full MIMO-OFDM channel. Ray-tracing experiments show that the proposed method improves normalized mean square error (NMSE) over pilot-only and direct reconstruction baselines, supporting latent field prediction as an effective prior for sparse-pilot channel acquisition.
items.title_ko: JEPA 기반 MIMO-OFDM 채널 재구성을 위한 희소 파일럿 잠재 필드 예측
items.summary_ko: 완전한 채널 상태 정보(CSI)의 정확한 획득은 MIMO-OFDM 무선 시스템에 필수적이지만, 밀집 파일럿 기반 추정은 상당한 오버헤드를 발생시킵니다. 이 연구는 JEPA(Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture)에서 영감을 받은 잠재 필드 예측 방법을 사용하여, 희소 파일럿으로부터 CSI를 효율적으로 재구성하는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 무선 통신 시스템에서 채널 추정의 효율성과 정확성을 향상시켜, 5G/6G 통신, 자율 주행 차량 통신 등 미래 무선 기술 발전에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution
items.body: Language model performance depends strongly on the mixture of domains in the pretraining data corpus. Popular data mixing methods select these domain weights by training many small proxy models on random mixes and then fitting a regression model to predict performance from the mix. We recognize this practice as a domain attribution problem, where the regression measures each domain's contribution to the target metric. Through this lens, the standard Dirichlet sampling of proxy data mixes is a poor regression design that requires tuning and cannot support a linear fit for hundreds of domains. Building on classical optimal experimental design, we introduce LinMix, which samples mixes at the vertices of the capped simplex so that each domain is at its cap or absent. This hyperparameter-free vertex sampling decorrelates domain effects, enabling an interpretable linear model whose coefficients are the domain attributions. The optimal mix given by LinMix provably keeps only domains with positive attribution values and requires no search over candidate mixes. We further establish the optimality of vertex sampling, and prove that Dirichlet sampling inflates the attribution error when its mixes concentrate around the prior data mix. Pretraining experiments with 1B-parameter OLMo2 and 4B Qwen3.5 language models show that LinMix outperforms Dirichlet-based data mixing across reasoning, code, and math benchmarks, with relative gains of 46% on MBPP and 14% on GSM8K. At 288 fine-grained domains, only vertex sampling supports a linear fit, and LinMix improves benchmark accuracy by 11% on average over the best nonlinear baseline.
items.title_ko: LinMix: 선형 도메인 귀인으로서의 데이터 혼합
items.summary_ko: 언어 모델 성능은 사전 학습 데이터 코퍼스의 도메인 혼합에 크게 의존합니다. 인기 있는 데이터 혼합 방법은 많은 작은 프록시 모델을 무작위 혼합으로 훈련하고, 성능을 혼합에서 예측하기 위해 회귀 모델을 적합시켜 도메인 가중치를 선택합니다. 이 연구는 이 관행을 각 도메인이 대상 메트릭에 기여하는 정도를 측정하는 도메인 귀인 문제로 인식합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 사전 학습 데이터셋 구성 및 최적화에 대한 새로운 관점을 제시하여, 모델 성능을 향상시키는 데 효과적인 데이터 혼합 전략을 개발하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

items.title: How Many and How Much? Contrastive Learning with Negative Samples for Knowledge Graph Embedding
items.body: Knowledge graph embedding (KGE), a fundamental technique for knowledge-centric Web and KG-augmented AI applications, is commonly trained through contrastive learning with negative samples to learn discriminative representations. Despite its empirical success, two crucial questions regarding negative samples remain underexplored: (Q1) how many negative samples should be used for each positive sample and (Q2) how much should each negative sample contribute to learning? To answer these questions, we propose RADAR, a novel contrastive learning framework for KGE models with two effective strategies, respectively: (1) Risk-aware negative budget allocation quantifies false-negative sampling risk by modeling an open-world KG as a stochastic partial observation of its closed-world counterpart and adaptively assigns a negative budget to each positive sample based on its risk; (2) Distribution-calibrated negative weighting assigns negative weights by calibrating the weighting strength for each positive based on two complementary characteristics of the negative-score distribution: dispersion and concentration. Extensive experiments on 3 real-world KGs with 4 KGE models reveal that RADAR achieves the best KGE performance on average across all model--KG combinations and reduces sampled false negatives by over 90% compared with conventional fixed-budget methods.
items.title_ko: 얼마나 많이, 그리고 얼마나? 지식 그래프 임베딩을 위한 네거티브 샘플을 이용한 대조 학습
items.summary_ko: 지식 그래프 임베딩(KGE)은 지식 중심 웹 및 KG 증강 AI 애플리케이션의 기본 기술이며, 일반적으로 네거티브 샘플을 이용한 대조 학습을 통해 훈련됩니다. 이 연구는 네거티브 샘플의 수와 각 네거티브 샘플이 학습에 기여해야 하는 정도라는 두 가지 핵심 질문을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 지식 그래프 임베딩 모델의 효율성과 성능을 향상시키는 데 중요한 네거티브 샘플링 전략에 대한 깊이 있는 이해를 제공합니다.

items.title: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks
items.body: It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network. In this work, we develop a more accurate approximation that is \emph{slightly} non-Gaussian, which we call the para-Gaussian distribution and is constructed from the Hermite polynomials. We show how this para-Gaussian approximation can lead to a practical recursive method to approximate the deeper layers of the network. Finally, we apply this theory to linear neural networks (where things can be solved exactly) and to ReLU neural networks (where things can be approximated).
items.title_ko: 무작위 심층 신경망의 준가우스 근사
items.summary_ko: 무작위로 초기화된 신경망은 $n\to \infty$ 극한에서 가우스 행동을 보이는 것으로 알려져 있습니다. 그러나 이 근사는 유한한 $n$에 대해서는 좋지 않으며, 네트워크가 깊어질수록 나빠집니다. 이 연구는 헤르미트 다항식으로 구성된, '약간' 비가우스적인 더 정확한 근사, 즉 준가우스 분포를 개발합니다.
items.why_ko: 심층 신경망의 이론적 분석을 개선하고, 유한한 깊이의 네트워크에서 동작을 더 정확하게 예측할 수 있는 수학적 도구를 제공합니다.

items.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
items.body: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. Because most intermediate channels in a routed expert contribute little to any single token, channel selectors predict which channels matter and read only their weights, typically keeping channels above a threshold calibrated on offline data. We show that channel selection needs no calibration data. First, a calibrated threshold does not fix how much a selector reads, because the number of channels passing it varies across inputs; Prox with thresholds calibrated for an 18% read budget actually reads only 12.9% on average across our benchmarks. Second, top-k keeps each token's k highest-scoring channels and needs no calibration data. At the calibrated budget, a selector's top-k version matches or beats its threshold version on the same score in 40 of 43 comparisons at 13% and 18% budgets, including all 23 on generation tasks. The top-k versions also avoid the repetition-loop collapse that calibrated thresholds cause on Gemma 4. Calibrating a threshold thus provides neither of the two things selectors use it for: a known read budget and a consistent accuracy gain at that budget. We furthermore introduce a reader built entirely from the model's weights, which screens channels with a ternary sketch and recovers the skipped ones with a low-rank map. Across three post-trained MoE models, our reader retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of routed-expert reads, with Triton kernels running MoE blocks 1.60 to 1.90x faster than optimized vLLM at batch one and up to 2.69x at larger batches on the same three models.
items.title_ko: MoE 디코딩을 위한 채널 선택은 보정 데이터가 필요 없다
items.summary_ko: MoE(Mixture-of-Experts) 모델은 작은 배치 크기에서 대화형 디코딩 중 라우팅된 전문가 가중치를 메모리에서 로드하는 것이 병목 현상입니다. 이 연구는 라우팅된 전문가의 대부분의 중간 채널이 어떤 단일 토큰에도 거의 기여하지 않기 때문에, 채널 선택기가 어떤 채널이 중요한지 예측하고 해당 가중치만 읽는다고 설명합니다. 그리고 채널 선택에는 보정 데이터가 필요 없음을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: MoE 모델의 추론 효율성을 크게 향상시키고, 특히 메모리 제약이 있는 환경에서 모델을 더 빠르게 배포하고 실행할 수 있는 실용적인 방법을 제공합니다.

items.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
items.body: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.
items.title_ko: PDRVLA: 물리적 동역학 표현을 가진 시각-언어-행동 모델
items.summary_ko: VLA(Vision-Language-Action) 모델은 시각적 관찰 및 언어 지시로부터 로봇 행동을 생성하지만, 물리적 동역학에 대한 이해는 제한적입니다. PDRVLA는 경량 물리 동역학 모듈이 시각-언어 특징으로부터 물리 토큰을 추출하여 온라인 비디오 생성 없이 행동 생성을 조건화합니다. 이 모듈은 물리적 동역학을 학습합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 복잡한 물리적 환경에서 더 지능적으로 행동하고 상호작용할 수 있도록 물리적 동역학 이해를 강화하여, 로봇 공학 분야의 발전에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences
items.body: Fact-checking explanations help Web users understand why a claim receives its verdict, yet the same explanation may not satisfy readers with different backgrounds and preferences. We formulate Faithful Personalized Fact-Checking Explanation Rewriting, which adapts an existing explanation to individual readers while preserving factual fidelity. Rather than relying on reader-written reference explanations, we learn personalized rewriting from the relative preferences of LLM-simulated readers. However, this presents two challenges: distinguishing persona-specific preferences from general explanation quality and learning beyond a limited set of predefined explanation styles. To address these challenges, we propose Personalized Explanation Rewriting via Preference Learning (PERPL), a framework consisting of two components. Simulated Preference Construction derives persona-specific supervision from simulated reader preferences through cross-persona reciprocal pairing. Progressive Preference Learning first trains a lightweight rewriter on the constructed supervision and then refines it through exploration-guided preference optimization, enabling it to discover preferred explanations beyond the predefined styles. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PERPL outperforms much larger general-purpose LLMs in personalized preference alignment while maintaining high factual fidelity.
items.title_ko: 같은 판단, 다른 독자: 상대적 선호도에서 팩트체크 설명 개인화
items.summary_ko: 팩트체크 설명은 웹 사용자가 주장이 왜 그런 판단을 받는지 이해하는 데 도움이 되지만, 동일한 설명이 다른 배경과 선호도를 가진 독자를 만족시키지 못할 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 '충실한 개인화된 팩트체크 설명 재작성'을 공식화하여, 사실적 충실도를 유지하면서 기존 설명을 개별 독자에게 맞게 조정합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 기반 팩트체크 시스템의 사용자 경험을 개선하고, 다양한 독자층의 정보 이해도를 높이는 데 중요한 기여를 합니다.

items.title: Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model
items.body: Generating several solutions can expose alternative methods, but additional trajectories often paraphrase one dominant approach. We investigate whether the conditional capacity of a frozen sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) model can provide such diversity from one problem prompt, without user-assigned roles, prescribed methods, fine-tuning, or model copies. Agent-Conditioned Routing (ACR) assigns $m$ parallel trajectories persistent, untrained shared/private expert-eligibility masks while preserving the learned, input-dependent token router. On a screened 126-question multi-mode mathematics and physics benchmark, with model judges reading the reported derivations in full, we count the number of problems yielding at least two distinct primary methods among soft-correct solutions in four trajectories. ACR reaches approximately twice as many such problems as the strongest temperature setting under GLM 5.3 (37.3 versus 18.7), and 1.67 times as many under GPT-5.6 Sol (45.00 versus 27.00), at matched output budgets. A blinded four-expert audit on a stratified sample of 30 problems also finds more multi-method solutions with ACR on both backbones, with lower correctness. Matched-eligibility ablations show modest multi-method count advantages for ACR, while token-resampled masks attain higher correctness. An informed sequential prompt elicits more diversity still, using previous solutions and explicit requests for alternative methods. ACR adds about 160 KiB of mask state. In a three-problem microbenchmark capped at 1,024 tokens, its latency and peak VRAM usage remain within 3% of batched temperature sampling.
items.title_ko: 에이전트 조건부 라우팅: 하나의 고정된 모델 내에서 다양한 추론 경로
items.summary_ko: 여러 솔루션을 생성하는 것은 대안적인 방법을 드러낼 수 있지만, 추가 궤적은 종종 하나의 지배적인 접근 방식을 바꾸어 말합니다. 이 연구는 고정된 희소 혼합-전문가(MoE) 모델의 조건부 용량이 사용자 지정 역할, 정해진 방법, 미세 조정 또는 모델 복사본 없이도 하나의 문제 프롬프트에서 그러한 다양성을 제공할 수 있는지 조사합니다.
items.why_ko: MoE 모델이 단일 프롬프트에 대해 여러 가지 다양한 추론 경로를 생성할 수 있도록 하여, AI 모델의 창의성과 문제 해결 능력을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Euclidean Crowding-Driven Adaptive Euclidean-Hyperbolic Graph Learning
items.body: Hyperbolic graph representation learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for modeling hierarchical data. Unlike Euclidean space, which exhibits polynomial volume growth, hyperbolic space grows exponentially with radius, naturally accommodating tree-like structures without the geometric distortion known as Euclidean crowding. Despite strong empirical performance, the theoretical mechanisms underlying hyperbolic embeddings remain poorly understood. In this work, we provide a geometric quantifcation research for Euclidean crowding, a generalization-theoretic explanation for the superiority of hyperbolic space on hierarchical data, and further develop an adaptive Euclidean-hyperbolic fusion learning framework toward bridging this gap. Specifically, we \textbf{first} establish a geometric quantification of Euclidean crowding by analyzing layer-wise minimum separation in node embeddings, proving that fixed-dimensional Euclidean embeddings of tree-like graphs inevitably exhibit layer-wise crowding that leads to weaker margin-based generalization bounds. \textbf{Second}, we provide a generalization-bound for the superiority of hyperbolic geometry on hierarchical data. \textbf{Third}, we propose EH-Fusion, a geometry-adaptive framework that lifts Euclidean GNN representations into hyperbolic space via exponential mapping and adaptively fuses both geometries based on node-level neighborhood expansion patterns. Extensive experiments validate our theoretical insights and demonstrate the effectiveness of EH-Fusion on benchmark datasets.
items.title_ko: 유클리드 혼잡 구동 적응형 유클리드-하이퍼볼릭 그래프 학습
items.summary_ko: 하이퍼볼릭 그래프 표현 학습은 계층적 데이터를 모델링하는 강력한 패러다임으로 부상했습니다. 이 연구는 유클리드 공간과 달리 반경에 따라 기하급수적으로 성장하는 하이퍼볼릭 공간이 나무와 같은 구조를 '유클리드 혼잡' 없이 자연스럽게 수용한다는 점에 주목합니다. 이 연구는 하이퍼볼릭 임베딩의 이론적 메커니즘을 기하학적으로 정량화합니다.
items.why_ko: 그래프 신경망이 계층적 데이터를 더 효과적으로 모델링하고, 복잡한 네트워크 구조를 이해하는 데 새로운 관점과 도구를 제공합니다.

items.title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
items.body: Deep learning algorithms have become widely used and successful across a wide range of tasks. A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data. In this theoretical work, we explore a new geometric structure defined on the data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix (DIM), a variation of the Fisher Information Matrix. This new geometric structure is a foliation and the main focus of this work is to explore the non-smooth case of ReLU activation functions, where traditional geometric tools often fail. The foliation is defined through a distribution spanned by the columns of the DIM. We first prove that this distribution is non-smooth in the sense of distributions, rendering the existence of an associated foliation much more complex. To circumvent this issue, we introduce a smoothed version of this distribution that differs from the original only on a set of measure zero. Finally, we prove that this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the data space, which is based on the data the network has been trained with. Our theoretical contributions provide a geometric framework to better understand how neural networks organize their input space in non-smooth settings, bridging differential geometry and deep learning theory.
items.title_ko: 매니폴드 학습의 기하학: 딥러닝 모델을 통한 특이점 층화
items.summary_ko: 딥러닝 알고리즘은 다양한 작업에서 널리 사용되고 성공적입니다. 중요한 과제는 이러한 알고리즘이 훈련 데이터의 내재적 기하학을 진정으로 포착하는지 여부를 결정하여 데이터에서 무엇을 배우는지 더 잘 이해하는 것입니다. 이 이론적 연구는 훈련된 신경망에 의해 데이터 정보 행렬(DIM)을 통해 데이터 공간에 정의된 새로운 기하학적 구조를 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 딥러닝 모델이 데이터를 학습하는 방식을 기하학적으로 해석하여, 모델의 블랙박스 특성을 이해하고 보다 이론적으로 견고한 AI 모델을 구축하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are usually evaluated by final-output correctness or safety, yet an endpoint label does not reveal how a failure develops throughout the reasoning process. We therefore ask whether ordinary reasoning failures and adversarially induced failures can be characterized using the same internal coordinates. Towards this end, we in this paper study a white-box diagnostic framework CauTrace to disclose the root-cause of why LLM fails from three fundamental inspections: Functional States, Propagation of Representation, Temporal-State Coordination and Reasoning Trajectory. First, seven functional states are creatively defined to represent the support and constraint processing in LLMs. Second, the propagation of representation change measures how the changes among the seven states persist across subsequent Transformer blocks. Third, temporal-state coordination and trajectory topology characterize when the commitment and verification occur relative to the support, and how the dominant state sequence evolves over the full inference process. Finally, we evaluate CauTrace on both clean reasoning failures and paired adversarial perturbations. Across Qwen and LLaMA-family models, the failed traces show weaker Attention-MLP agreement on support-state updates and less verification activity relative to commitment, while the exact representation-level signatures and timing shifts vary by architecture. Held-out repair and steering tests demonstrate consistent operational signals that were in line with our claims for certain models and specific settings, with aligned steering producing the predicted directional changes in process measures. Overall, CauTrace provides a unified diagnostic framework for analyzing failure dynamics through changes in support, commitment, and verification, which would shed light on the in-depth research on LLM security.
items.title_ko: LLM이 실패하는 이유 밝히기: 내부 메커니즘에서 적대적 추론 궤적까지
items.summary_ko: LLM은 일반적으로 최종 출력의 정확성이나 안전성으로 평가되지만, 끝점 레이블은 추론 과정 전반에 걸쳐 실패가 어떻게 발생하는지 드러내지 않습니다. 이 논문은 내부 메커니즘과 적대적 추론 궤적을 통해 LLM이 실패하는 근본 원인을 밝히는 'CauTrace'라는 화이트박스 진단 프레임워크를 연구합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 실패 원인을 진단하고 분석하는 체계적인 방법을 제공하여, 모델의 신뢰성과 견고성을 향상시키는 데 필수적인 정보를 제공합니다.

items.title: TRIDENT-Seq: Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast for Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling
items.body: Ant International accumulates large volumes of transaction history across users and payment businesses. Confirmed fraud and chargeback outcomes, by contrast, are scarce, delayed, and specific to each business. A single encoder pretrained on unlabeled histories could serve all businesses, but only if pretraining captures the behavior that separates risk. Coarse activity differences can make contrastive pretraining on transaction logs too easy: transaction volume, amount, and timing can distinguish a history's continuation from arbitrary candidates without modeling how payment resources are used. We present TRIDENT-Seq, a transaction foundation model trained with Prefix-Future Contrast (PFC). PFC matches each prefix to a summary of its subsequent behavior among candidates with similar activity profiles; activity prediction and dispersion regularization act on the encoder output. Across three production payment businesses, the pretrained encoder improves average precision (AP) and recall at a 0.5% intervention budget over architecture-matched scratch training in all six business-budget settings. With a fixed validation set, it exceeds full-label scratch training in mean AP and recall using 10% of the training labels on Wallet and 25% on Shopping and SME. Pretraining only on another business's histories still helps. Replacing profile-matched candidates with random ones cuts recall from 24.62% to 5.64%. In Ant International's deployment evaluation, recorded amount-based chargeback and overall loss rates are 37.7% and 37.9% lower than those of the previous XGBoost-based system under the same intervention budget.
items.title_ko: TRIDENT-Seq: 레이블 효율적인 결제 위험 모델링을 위한 프로필 일치 접두사-미래 대비
items.summary_ko: Ant International은 사용자 및 결제 사업 전반에 걸쳐 대량의 거래 내역을 축적하지만, 확인된 사기 및 차지백 결과는 드물고 지연되며 각 사업에 특정합니다. TRIDENT-Seq는 레이블 효율적인 결제 위험 모델링을 위한 프로필 일치 접두사-미래 대비 방법을 제안하여, 레이블링되지 않은 내역으로 사전 학습된 단일 인코더가 모든 사업에 서비스할 수 있도록 합니다.
items.why_ko: 금융 사기 탐지 및 위험 관리 분야에서 AI 모델의 레이블링 효율성을 높여, 제한된 레이블 데이터로도 정확한 예측을 가능하게 합니다.

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
items.body: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. Furthermore, our design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights. We present ablations analyzing key decisions and release EmbeddingGemma 2 to promote further research.
items.body_ko: 우리는 텍스트, 이미지, 오디오, 비디오 및 이들의 조합을 통합된 공간에서 기본적으로 표현하는 개방형 멀티모달 임베딩 모델인 EmbeddingGemma 2를 선보입니다. 우리의 접근 방식은 단순화된 계층별 임베딩과 모달리티 및 목표 진행을 포함한 다단계 커리큘럼과 같은 개선 사항을 도입하여 단일 모달, 교차 모달 및 혼합 모달 평가 전반에 걸쳐 강력한 품질을 보장합니다. 특히, 모든 모달리티에 걸친 포괄적인 임베딩 벤치마크에서 EmbeddingGemma 2는 새로운 파레토 프론티어를 구축하여 전문 모델과 두 배에서 열두 배 더 큰 모델을 모두 능가합니다. 또한, 우리의 설계는 리소스가 제한된 환경에 대한 유연성을 제공하며, 선택적 모달리티 인코더 로딩, 조정 가능한 비전 토큰 예산, 절단 가능한 임베딩 차원 및 양자화된 가중치를 지원합니다. 우리는 주요 결정 사항을 분석하는 제거 연구를 제시하고 추가 연구를 촉진하기 위해 EmbeddingGemma 2를 공개합니다.
items.title_ko: EmbeddingGemma 2: 통합되고 효율적인 멀티모달 표현
items.summary_ko: EmbeddingGemma 2는 텍스트, 이미지, 오디오, 비디오 및 이들의 조합을 통합된 공간에서 기본적으로 표현하는 오픈 멀티모달 임베딩 모델입니다. 이 접근 방식은 단순화된 계층별 임베딩과 모달리티 및 목표 진행을 포함하는 다단계 커리큘럼을 통해 단일 모달, 교차 모달 및 혼합 모달 평가 전반에 걸쳐 강력한 품질을 보장합니다.
items.why_ko: 다양한 모달리티(텍스트, 이미지, 오디오, 비디오)를 하나의 통합된 임베딩 공간에 표현하는 것은 진정한 멀티모달 AI 시스템 개발의 핵심 단계이며, 이는 다양한 AI 애플리케이션의 성능을 크게 향상시킬 것입니다.

items.title: Online Interval Selection with Binary Predictions: Optimal Consistency and a Continuous Robustness Tradeoff
items.body: We study online interval selection with binary predictions of membership in a final optimal solution. Requests arrive in arbitrary order; accepted requests may be revoked, but rejected or revoked requests cannot be recovered. With rewards proportional to interval length, the best consistency under finite strict robustness is $d=(3+\sqrt5)/2$ when both guarantees hold almost surely on each fixed input, including for randomized algorithms. A continuous lower bound forces consistency strictly above $d$ at every robustness budget below $4\varphi+3\approx9.472$, whereas our deterministic algorithm attains $d$ with exact robustness $\varphi^5\approx11.090$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Each held interval inherits a ledger recording positive prediction mass lost through irrevocable decisions. A tunable replacement cost gives a continuous family with exact consistency throughout and exact robustness on two parameter intervals, including $(C,R)=(25/9,10)$ and $(4,7)$. Randomization permits expected consistency approaching one with finite expected robustness, whereas almost-sure robustness forces expected consistency strictly above two at every finite budget.
items.title_ko: 이진 예측을 통한 온라인 구간 선택: 최적의 일관성 및 연속적인 견고성 상충
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 최종 최적 솔루션에 대한 멤버십의 이진 예측을 통한 온라인 구간 선택을 연구합니다. 요청은 임의의 순서로 도착하며, 수락된 요청은 철회될 수 있지만, 거부되거나 철회된 요청은 복구할 수 없습니다. 구간 길이에 비례하는 보상으로, 유한한 엄격한 견고성 하의 최적 일관성은 $d=(3+\sqrt5)/2$입니다.
items.why_ko: 온라인 의사결정 알고리즘의 이론적 한계와 성능 상충 관계를 이해하는 데 도움이 되며, 실시간 자원 관리 및 스케줄링 문제에 대한 해결책을 설계하는 데 유용합니다.

items.title: Aligning Institutional Power and Operational Ability
items.body: To be socially sustainable, Agentic AI systems require normative designs that align responsibilities with the ability to fulfil them. Identifying incongruences such as unsatisfiable expectations or privilege escalation is crucial in avoiding normative pitfalls. In this study, we discuss design dimensions suitable for describing multi-agent systems in light of this norm-ability alignment requirement. We propose a formal framework centred on process-oriented modelling and institutional power for the analysis of a given normatively relevant process, discuss strategies for repairing it, and elaborate on how the symmetrical relation between operational process and institutional state affects the lifecycle of normative positions.
items.title_ko: 기관 권한과 운영 능력 정렬
items.summary_ko: 사회적으로 지속 가능한 에이전트 AI 시스템은 책임과 이행 능력을 일치시키는 규범적 설계를 요구합니다. 충족할 수 없는 기대치나 권한 에스컬레이션과 같은 불일치를 식별하는 것은 규범적 함정을 피하는 데 중요합니다. 이 연구는 이러한 규범-능력 정렬 요구 사항을 고려하여 다중 에이전트 시스템을 설명하는 데 적합한 설계 차원을 논의합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트 시스템의 윤리적이고 사회적으로 책임 있는 설계를 위한 프레임워크를 제공하여, AI 기술의 신뢰성 있는 배포 및 거버넌스에 기여합니다.

items.title: Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection
items.body: Web-enabled digital health services are expanding access to physiological monitoring and mental health screening. However, electroencephalography (EEG)-based major depressive disorder (MDD) detection remains challenging across heterogeneous data sources, where individual variability and acquisition differences may affect disease-related representations. In this work, we investigate the use of healthy normative references for EEG-based MDD detection. Specifically, structural and distributional reference models are independently trained using healthy control (HC) recordings to characterize departures from healthy EEG patterns. We develop two diagnostic approaches that incorporate normative deviations at different representation levels. Scalar-level Normative Deviation-guided Diagnosis (S-NDD) summarizes structural and distributional deviations into scalar scores and integrates them with deep EEG representations. Feature-level Normative Deviation-guided Diagnosis (F-NDD) retains dimension-wise residuals and combines them with deep EEG representations through attention-based aggregation and auxiliary supervision. We also employ target HC-assisted score calibration for cross-source evaluation without updating the trained models. Experiments on two public EEG datasets examine both approaches under subject-independent within-source and bidirectional cross-source settings. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of normative deviation-guided diagnosis across different evaluation settings.
items.title_ko: EEG 기반 우울증 탐지를 위한 규범적 편차 모델링
items.summary_ko: 웹 기반 디지털 건강 서비스는 생체 신호 모니터링 및 정신 건강 검진에 대한 접근성을 확장하고 있습니다. 그러나 EEG(뇌전도) 기반 주요 우울 장애(MDD) 탐지는 이질적인 데이터 소스 전반에 걸쳐 여전히 어렵습니다. 이 연구는 EEG 기반 MDD 탐지를 위한 건강한 규범적 참조(normative references) 사용을 조사합니다.
items.why_ko: 정신 건강 분야에서 AI 기반 진단 도구의 정확성을 향상시키고, 이질적인 데이터 환경에서도 신뢰할 수 있는 우울증 탐지 시스템 개발에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) require substantial memory, motivating low-bit weight quantization for efficient deployment. Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods often improve accuracy by increasing the effective coding dimension, which can complicate independent lookup and local codeword updates. We propose CoS-VQ (Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization), which preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and their shared scale across positions. The key challenge is scale-induced coupling: the optimal scale depends on the entire codeword combination and, in turn, changes candidate rankings across positions, so pointwise updates can stall even after scale re-optimization. CoS-VQ collects candidates at multiple probe scales and constructs a tangent separable upper bound for the residual-aware quadratic objective. By reducing candidate comparisons to lower envelopes of lines over positive scales, it identifies finitely many representative intervals for joint index--scale updates without exhaustively enumerating codeword combinations. On Qwen3.8-27B, CoS-VQ outperforms QTIP and LLVQ on the evaluated language modeling, coding, and reasoning benchmarks. Ablations from the same initialization further show larger gains from joint updates than from scale-only refinement, highlighting joint selection as an alternative to increasing codeword dimensionality. The code is available at https://github.com/xzktx003/Cos_VQ.
items.title_ko: CoS-VQ: 대규모 언어 모델을 위한 공동 조정된 공유 스케일 벡터 양자화
items.summary_ko: LLM은 상당한 메모리를 필요로 하여 효율적인 배포를 위해 저비트 가중치 양자화가 중요합니다. 기존 벡터 양자화(VQ) 방법은 유효 코딩 차원을 늘려 정확도를 향상시키지만, 독립적인 조회 및 로컬 코드워드 업데이트를 복잡하게 만들 수 있습니다. CoS-VQ는 저차원 코드워드를 유지하면서 하드 인덱스와 위치 전반의 공유 스케일을 공동으로 최적화합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 메모리 사용량을 줄이고 추론 효율성을 높여, 자원 제약이 있는 환경(예: 엣지 디바이스)에서 대규모 모델을 배포하고 실행하는 데 필요한 실용적인 방법을 제공합니다.

items.title: WCC: A Learning-Based Framework for Deciding When to Apply Cooperative Coevolution in Large-Scale Optimization
items.body: Cooperative Coevolution (CC) and Non-Decomposition Algorithms (NDAs) are two primary approaches for large-scale global optimization (LSGO). Although both have achieved success, they exhibit markedly different performance across problem types and each faces approach-specific limitations, leaving the question of "when to use CC" unresolved. We address this gap with WCC, a novel learning-based framework that dynamically decides when to deploy CC in LSGO. WCC employs a streamlined design for efficient adaptive learning. We formulate the decision as a Markov decision process, designing a targeted feature set, a robust reward, and a tailored network architecture to provide the agent with rich information about the problem state and optimization progress. Our auto-regressive policy enables WCC to perform fine-grained, dynamic switching between CC and NDAs while conditionally allocating the computational budget without expert specifications. WCC shows strong competitiveness and superior generalization across problems, optimization horizons, and baseline optimizers. It realizes a "train-once and reuse" paradigm under a low budget, significantly curbing LSGO cost. Additionally, in-depth analyses yield insights not captured by existing theory, offering practical guidance on when and how to effectively deploy CC.
items.title_ko: 대규모 최적화에서 협력적 공진화(CC) 적용 시점을 결정하는 학습 기반 프레임워크 WCC
items.summary_ko: WCC는 대규모 전역 최적화(LSGO) 문제에서 협력적 공진화(CC)와 비분해 알고리즘(NDA) 중 어떤 접근 방식을 사용할지 동적으로 결정하는 학습 기반 프레임워크입니다. 이 프레임워크는 문제 유형에 따라 상이한 성능을 보이는 두 접근 방식의 한계를 해결하기 위해 설계되었습니다. 효율성을 위해 간소화된 설계를 특징으로 합니다.
items.why_ko: 최적화 문제에서 어떤 알고리즘을 적용할지 효율적으로 결정하는 것은 계산 비용 절감과 성능 향상에 중요한 실무적 함의를 가집니다.

items.title: Scale-aware and spatially-localised optimisation of kilometre-scale MLWP models
items.body: Preserving fine-scale structure without degrading spatial accuracy is a central challenge for kilometre-scale machine-learning weather prediction (MLWP). We introduce a loss based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform that constrains atmospheric fields jointly by scale, location, and orientation. We evaluate its performance using an experimental joint global--regional FastNet configuration, which produces \SI{1.5}{km} forecasts over the UK alongside $\sim$\SI{31}{km} global forecasts. Relative to both mean-squared error (MSE) and an FFT-based spectral objective, the wavelet loss substantially improves spectral fidelity. Compared with MSE training, it maintains similar pointwise performance, improves neighbourhood-based verification, and produces sharper precipitation fields with more realistic intensity distributions. These results demonstrate that spatially localised wavelet constraints can preserve multiscale atmospheric structure while largely avoiding the loss of pointwise accuracy associated with globally supported spectral objectives.
items.title_ko: 킬로미터 스케일 기계 학습 기상 예측(MLWP) 모델의 스케일 인식 및 공간 국지화 최적화
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 킬로미터 스케일 기계 학습 기상 예측(MLWP)에서 공간 정확도를 저하시키지 않으면서 미세 스케일 구조를 보존하는 문제를 다룹니다. 이중 트리 복소 웨이블릿 변환 기반 손실 함수를 도입하여 대기장을 스케일, 위치, 방향에 따라 동시에 제약합니다. 영국 상공의 1.5km 예측과 약 31km의 전역 예측을 생성하는 실험적인 FastNet 구성으로 성능을 평가합니다.
items.why_ko: 정확한 기상 예측 모델은 기후 변화 연구 및 재난 예방에 필수적이며, 미세 스케일 구조를 보존하는 최적화 기법은 모델의 실용성을 크게 향상시킬 수 있습니다.

items.title: UCVE: Graph Structured Retrieval for Compliance Validation
items.body: Structured compliance validation requires determining whether every obligation in a predefined requirement space is satisfied, violated, or unaddressed by a given document. This can be described as a coverage problem that existing retrieval and classification systems, by treating requirements as independent, are not designed to solve. We introduce \textbf{\ac{UCVE}}, a domain-agnostic framework that represents compliance requirement spaces as a \ac{CRG} and performs retrieval via spectral reranking over its reinforcement learning-weighted Laplacian. Edges between requirement nodes are learned via reinforcement learning with a traversal reward grounded in violation detection, reshaping the graph's community structure such that low-pass spectral filtering distinguishes relevant from irrelevant obligation clusters. Evaluating across three compliance domains, \ac{UCVE} averages 4.3\% matched-$K$ recall lift over flat cosine retrieval and consistently outperforms strong retrieval and graph-based baselines.
items.title_ko: 규정 준수 검증을 위한 그래프 기반 정보 검색 프레임워크 UCVE
items.summary_ko: UCVE는 구조화된 규정 준수 검증을 위해 설계된 도메인 불가지론적 프레임워크입니다. 이 시스템은 요구사항 공간을 CRG(Compliance Requirement Graph)로 표현하고 스펙트럼 재순위 지정을 통해 검색을 수행하여 문서 내 모든 의무가 충족, 위반 또는 미해결되었는지 확인합니다. 기존 검색 및 분류 시스템이 개별 요구사항을 독립적으로 처리하는 한계를 극복합니다.
items.why_ko: 법률 및 규정 준수 검증은 기업 및 조직에 매우 중요하며, 이 프레임워크는 복잡한 문서에서 규정 준수 여부를 효율적이고 정확하게 판단하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있습니다.

items.title: AnalogScout: Simulation-Efficient PVT-Aware Analog Sizing with LLM Agents
items.body: Analog device sizing must satisfy all specifications across process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) corners to ensure tape-out success, but simulating every candidate at all corners dominates the sizing time and slows design iteration. Conventional surrogate-based optimizers search the sizing space directly, while recent large language model (LLM) agents add circuit knowledge to designs but still delegate the sizes to global optimizers. Both learn the circuit response from repeated multi-corner SPICE simulations and optimize on top of it, which becomes expensive under a limited simulation budget. Providing an agent with reusable verified designs and sizing sub-blocks analytically could save most of this budget. We propose AnalogScout, a simulation-efficient PVT-aware sizing framework driven by an LLM agent. Combining elite-design reuse, analytic gm/Id local sizing and global refinement under full-corner verification, AnalogScout reduces power by 43.3% relative to the evolution strategy CMA-ES at an equal budget of 16k simulations on three SKY130 OTAs of increasing complexity, and reaches the final CMA-ES power after 7.0% of that budget. It also attains lower power than Bayesian optimization on all three OTAs and than two re-implemented LLM-driven flows on the two OTAs where they were tested.
items.title_ko: LLM 에이전트를 활용한 시뮬레이션 효율적인 PVT 인식 아날로그 회로 설계 최적화 AnalogScout
items.summary_ko: AnalogScout은 프로세스, 전압, 온도(PVT) 변화에 강건한 아날로그 소자 설계를 위한 시뮬레이션 효율적인 접근 방식입니다. 기존 최적화 방식이 모든 PVT 코너에서 시뮬레이션을 반복해야 하는 비효율성을 개선하여 설계 시간을 단축합니다. 이 프레임워크는 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 에이전트를 활용하여 회로 지식을 설계에 통합하면서 최적화 과정을 가속화합니다.
items.why_ko: 아날로그 회로 설계는 반도체 개발의 핵심 요소이며, LLM 에이전트를 활용하여 설계 시간을 단축하는 것은 개발 생산성을 크게 향상시킬 수 있습니다.

items.title: ReForest: Interpretability Meets Reasoning in Isolation Forest
items.body: Statistical anomaly detection methods like Isolation Forest are efficient but suffer from a critical semantic gap. They identify numerical rarities but fail to understand the contextual meaning of data, often missing subtle, context-dependent anomalies. Conversely, Large Language Models possess strong semantic reasoning capabilities but are prohibitively expensive and slow for large-scale deployment. To bridge this gap, we propose ReForest, a novel framework that synergizes the statistical efficiency of Isolation Forest with the reasoning power of LLMs. ReForest transforms the latent decision paths of Isolation Forest into natural-language explanations, enabling an LLM to refine anomaly detection through an uncertainty-aware dynamic ensemble. This approach allows the model to adaptively weigh statistical and semantic signals based on uncertainty-driven instance-level confidence. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets (Healthcare, Finance) demonstrate that ReForest significantly outperforms baselines, achieving an average 21% improvement in Recall and a 10% gain in F1-score. Our framework not only improves detection performance but also enhances model transparency by grounding semantic narratives in statistical evidence, providing interpretable rationales essential for high-stakes decision-making.
items.title_ko: ReForest: Isolation Forest에 해석 가능성과 추론 능력 결합
items.summary_ko: ReForest는 통계적 이상 탐지 방법인 Isolation Forest의 효율성에 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)의 의미론적 추론 능력을 결합한 새로운 프레임워크입니다. Isolation Forest가 수치적 희귀성만 식별하고 문맥적 의미를 놓치는 한계를 극복하여 미묘하고 문맥 의존적인 이상 징후를 탐지합니다. LLM의 높은 비용과 속도 문제를 해결하기 위해 두 기술의 시너지를 활용합니다.
items.why_ko: 이상 탐지 모델의 해석 가능성과 문맥 이해 능력은 금융 사기, 시스템 오류 등 다양한 분야에서 실제 적용 가치를 높이는 중요한 연구 방향입니다.

items.title: A Lightweight Attention-Based CNN with Saliency-Map Interpretability for Skin Cancer Detection
items.body: Skin cancer is among the most prevalent and life threatening forms of cancer worldwide. Early and accurate diagnosis significantly improves patient survival rates. However, manual dermoscopic assessment remains challenging due to visual similarity. This study proposes an Explainable AI-driven framework for automated binary classification of skin lesions using a lightweight attention-based convolutional neural network (CNN-Attention). The model integrates channel attention to focus on informative regions of dermoscopic images while maintaining low computational complexity. A publicly available dataset comprising 2,637 training and 660 test images was used, with balanced class weights. The proposed model achieved 87 percent accuracy with 1.95 million parameters and 7.45 MB of storage, matching the best baseline (MobileNet) while using approximately half as many parameters and half as much storage. ROC AUC and PR AUC scores reached 0.9475 and 0.9430, respectively. Additionally, saliency maps were incorporated as an explainability technique to visualize regions that influence model decisions. Comparative analysis with VGG16,VGG19,ResNet101,and MobileNet demonstrates the proposed models effectiveness in balancing classification results, computational efficiency, and interpretability.
items.title_ko: 피부암 진단을 위한 경량 주의 기반 CNN 및 살리언시 맵 해석 가능성 연구
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 조기 진단이 중요한 피부암의 자동 이진 분류를 위한 설명 가능한 AI 프레임워크를 제안합니다. 경량의 주의 기반 CNN(CNN-Attention) 모델은 채널 주의 메커니즘을 통합하여 정보성 특징에 집중하며, 살리언시 맵을 통해 모델의 예측을 시각적으로 해석할 수 있도록 합니다. 이는 수동 피부경 검사의 어려움을 개선하고자 합니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 AI 분야에서 모델의 결정 과정을 설명하는 능력은 진단 신뢰도를 높이고 의료진의 수용성을 확보하는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: Structured Representation Probing for Risk Anticipation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.body: End-to-end driving policies form structured internal representations of traffic, ego behavior, and road constraints. These representations offer a monitoring interface for anticipating failures, complementing risk signals from trajectories, controls, and manually designed features. We introduce the Structured Representation Probe (SRP), a lightweight monitor that reads actor, ego, and map representations from a frozen policy. SRP learns a separate linear risk direction for each source and aggregates element scores through cardinality-normalized log-mean-exp pooling, retaining sensitivity to salient evidence while reducing dependence on token count. Event-window supervision links the readout to upcoming hard failures, and auxiliary event type heads jointly train the source directions across failure modes. Online alerting uses a single generic score without modifying the driving policy. Bench2Drive experiments on DriveTransformer, UniAD, and VAD show higher frame-level PR-AUC and ROC-AUC than the evaluated runtime baselines. On DriveTransformer at a horizon of 2 seconds, ROC-AUC reaches 0.833 versus 0.715 for temporal consistency, with 2.67% readout runtime overhead. The trained probes also retain the ability to distinguish impending failures on new routes.
items.title_ko: 자율주행의 리스크 예측을 위한 구조화된 내부 표현 탐색
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 종단 간 자율주행 정책이 트래픽, 자율 주행 차량의 행동, 도로 제약 조건에 대한 구조화된 내부 표현을 형성한다는 점에 주목합니다. Structured Representation Probe (SRP)라는 경량 모니터를 도입하여 정지된 정책에서 액터, 자율 주행 차량, 지도 표현을 읽어옵니다. SRP는 각 소스에 대해 별도의 선형 리스크 방향을 학습하고 이를 통합하여 실패를 예측합니다.
items.why_ko: 자율주행 시스템의 안전성은 매우 중요하며, 내부 표현을 활용하여 잠재적 실패를 미리 예측하는 것은 시스템의 신뢰성을 높이는 핵심 기술입니다.

items.title: Multi-Label Agreement: A Flexible Framework for Inter-Annotator Reliability
items.body:
Reliable evaluation of inter-annotator agreement (IAA) is important for assessing the consistency of annotation processes. While established IAA metrics such as Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha are commonly applied in single-label settings, multi-label tasks require additional decisions about how full label sets, joint selections, and joint omissions should be compared.
In this work, we present Multi-Label Agreement (MLA), a flexible framework for evaluating agreement in multi-label annotation tasks. MLA preserves the full binary label vectors assigned to each item and uses average pairwise Hamming agreement, thereby accounting for both joint selections and joint omissions. Its pooled-marginal form is not a mathematically independent coefficient: it is a chance-disagreement-weighted average of label-wise Fleiss/Scott-type coefficients and is closely related to Krippendorff's alpha with normalized Hamming distance. The framework supports pooled-marginal, Gwet AC1, and fixed-baseline normalizations, yields item-level, label-level, and corpus-level results, and includes a conditional minimum-agreement diagnostic. Through a worked example and Monte Carlo simulations, we show how the resulting values depend on label prevalence, the declared label inventory, and the selected model of expected agreement. We also provide a Python implementation. MLA thus offers a transparent and interpretable framework for multi-label agreement analysis without claiming that one normalization is universally preferable.
items.title_ko: 다중 레이블 주석자 간 신뢰도 평가를 위한 유연한 프레임워크 MLA
items.summary_ko: Multi-Label Agreement (MLA)는 다중 레이블 주석 작업에서 주석자 간 일치도(IAA)를 평가하기 위한 유연한 프레임워크입니다. 기존의 단일 레이블 IAA 지표들이 다중 레이블 설정에서 발생하는 복잡성(전체 레이블 세트, 공동 선택, 공동 누락 비교 방식)을 해결하지 못하는 점을 개선합니다. 이를 통해 주석 프로세스의 일관성을 신뢰성 있게 평가할 수 있습니다.
items.why_ko: 데이터 주석의 품질은 AI 모델 성능에 직결되므로, 다중 레이블 환경에서 주석자 간 일치도를 정확히 측정하는 프레임워크는 고품질 데이터셋 구축에 필수적입니다.

items.title: Bayesian Inference of Expensive Simulators: Survey and Comparison of Design Choices
items.body:
We present a survey of approaches to Bayesian inference with simulator forward models, focusing on settings with prohibitively expensive simulators. In this domain, Bayesian optimization-based methods have emerged as the most promising approach. We unify existing methods into a general framework, enabling consistent reasoning about shared algorithmic structure across the fragmented literature. Within this framework, we identify the primary design choices and perform a systematic empirical comparison of their effects on inference efficiency in terms of required simulation budget.
A key result of our study is that inference efficiency is often dominated by the choice of surrogate-model response variable, as it directly governs the complexity of the modeled function. Specifically, we demonstrate that the prevalent scalar log-likelihood is a poor response variable, as it discards crucial information. Based on this insight, we introduce the concept of custom \emph{proxy variables}: transformations of simulator outputs engineered to retain more information and provide smoother response surfaces, substantially improving inference efficiency over standard response variables.
We provide actionable guidance and a numerically robust Julia package to facilitate practical adoption of Bayesian optimization for simulator inverse problems.
items.title_ko: 고비용 시뮬레이터의 베이즈 추론: 설계 선택 사항에 대한 설문 조사 및 비교
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 시뮬레이터 포워드 모델을 사용한 베이즈 추론 접근 방식들을 조사하며, 특히 시뮬레이션 비용이 높은 환경에 중점을 둡니다. 베이즈 최적화 기반 방법론들이 가장 유망한 접근 방식으로 부상했음을 밝히고, 기존 방법들을 통일된 프레임워크로 통합하여 공통된 알고리즘 구조를 일관성 있게 추론할 수 있도록 합니다. 이 프레임워크 내에서 주요 설계 선택 사항을 식별하고 체계적인 비교 분석을 수행합니다.
items.why_ko: 고비용 시뮬레이터를 사용하는 연구 및 개발 분야에서 베이즈 추론은 필수적인 도구이며, 이 연구는 효율적인 방법론 선택과 개선에 대한 실질적인 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: RPSD: Retrieval-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation with Optimal Transport
items.body: Sequential recommendation predicts a user's next interaction from historical behavior. Recent LLM-based methods recast this task as generative recommendation and increasingly adopt reinforcement learning such as GRPO for post-training. However, these methods suffer from two limitations, namely credit-blind optimization, where a sequence-level reward is shared across all generated tokens, and collaborative-blind supervision, where each training signal is derived from a single user and ignores behavioral patterns shared across similar users. To address both issues, we propose Retrieval-Privileged on-policy Self-Distillation (RPSD). For credit-blind optimization, we introduce on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), in which a teacher with privileged knowledge re-evaluates the student's on-policy response, and the token-level confidence difference between the student and teacher reshapes the shared sequence-level advantage into token-specific credit. However, the privileged knowledge in vanilla OPSD is still derived from a single user, leaving collaborative-blind supervision unresolved. We therefore ground the teacher in collaborative behavioral evidence from similar users. Specifically, we use temporally aware optimal transport (OT) to compare interaction trajectories across users by jointly considering item similarity and temporal structure, and further apply diversity-aware selection to retain complementary trajectories as privileged evidence. In this way, on-policy self-distillation provides fine-grained token-level credit, while OT enriches the teacher with structured cross-user evidence. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to bring on-policy self-distillation to sequential recommendation and to use cross-user behavior as its privileged signal. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that RPSD achieves state-of-the-art performance.
items.title_ko: 최적 수송을 이용한 검색 특권 온-정책 자가 증류 RPSD
items.summary_ko: RPSD는 사용자의 다음 상호작용을 예측하는 순차적 추천 시스템을 위한 새로운 방법론입니다. 기존 LLM 기반 추천 시스템의 두 가지 한계인 '크레딧 블라인드 최적화'와 '협력 블라인드 감독' 문제를 해결합니다. RPSD는 최적 수송(Optimal Transport) 개념을 활용하여 이러한 한계를 극복하고 추천 성능을 향상시킵니다.
items.why_ko: 추천 시스템은 사용자 경험에 직접적인 영향을 미치며, LLM 기반 모델의 한계를 극복하는 이 방법은 더욱 정확하고 개인화된 추천을 가능하게 할 것입니다.

items.title: Modeling Preference Dependencies with Directed Acyclic Graphs for Narrative-Driven Recommendation
items.body: Narrative-driven recommendation allows users to express multifaceted needs through free-form text where stated preferences naturally qualify and condition one another. Existing methods typically treat narratives as flat keyword combinations or unconstrained generative queries, failing to capture how complex preferences hierarchically refine and contextualize each other. We propose the Preference Dependency Graph Framework (PDG-F), a narrative-driven recommendation framework centered on explicit preference dependencies. Specifically, PDG-A (PDG-Agent) first parses unstructured requests to organize user preferences and their mutual qualifications into a directed acyclic Preference Dependency Graph (PDG). Through this graph, candidate evidence from the open Web is acquired via directed path retrieval, and final recommendations are determined by topological path ranking. Comprehensive experiments across three diverse domains spanning English and Chinese contexts confirm that PDG-F consistently achieves superior recommendation performance over competitive baselines, open-domain retrieval agents, and frontier language models. Further diagnostic analyses show that our dependency-guided retrieval markedly raises the attainable candidate-pool ceiling, demonstrating the fundamental value of modeling preference dependencies in narrative-driven recommendation.
items.title_ko: 내러티브 기반 추천을 위한 방향성 비순환 그래프를 이용한 선호도 종속성 모델링
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 사용자가 자유 형식 텍스트로 복합적인 선호도를 표현하는 내러티브 기반 추천 시스템에 초점을 맞춥니다. 기존 방식이 복잡한 선호도가 계층적으로 정제되고 문맥화되는 방식을 포착하지 못하는 한계를 지적하며, Preference Dependency Graph Framework (PDG-F)를 제안합니다. PDG-F는 명시적 선호도 종속성 그래프를 중심으로 내러티브 기반 추천을 수행합니다.
items.why_ko: 사용자의 복잡한 요구사항을 정확하게 이해하고 반영하는 추천 시스템은 개인화된 서비스 경험을 극대화하고, LLM 기반 추천 시스템의 발전 방향을 제시합니다.

items.title: Quoting Ted Sanders
items.body:
In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered:

Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra

[...] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7.

— Ted Sanders, explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions

Tags: generative-ai, gpt, openai, ai, llms, ted-sanders
items.title_ko: LLM 성능의 다차원성과 모델 크기의 중요성
items.summary_ko: LLM의 성능은 수학, 유머 등 다양한 차원에서 평가되며, 특정 작업에서 최고인 모델이 다른 작업에서도 최고일 것이라는 보장은 없습니다. 하지만 모델 크기가 성능 변화의 주요 변수이며, 일반적으로 모델이 클수록 성능과 신뢰성이 높고, 토큰당 비용이 비싸며, 이질적인 사실에 대한 기억력이 더 좋다는 점을 강조합니다. Luna, Terra, Sol, Astra 순으로 모델 크기가 커집니다.

items.title: GitHub Octoverse 2026
items.body:
GitHub Octoverse 2026

I'm at GitHub Universe today (GitHub gave me a free ticket through their "GitHub Stars" program). EVP Jay Parikh just announced this year's Octoverse report, and highlighted these numbers in particular:

This is a pretty stark representation of the impact of agentic engineering on GitHub. In 2026, merged pull requests tripled in less than a year to 220 million per month. Commits more than tripled to 7.38 billion per month, with most of that increase in the second half of this year. New repository rate doubled this year, to 30.3 million per month.

The report includes new numbers by industry, and breaks out numbers for repositories that involve "interoperability or reverse engineering". The methodology section includes notes about how they did this:

Top countries by pushes to public repositories, adjusted by profile location. Pushes from each country were summed across the Octoverse year. To adjust for biases caused by VPN usage, LLM classification was used to extract the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code from the profiles of GitHub users who contributed pushes during this period [...]

Industry. Public repositories created 2022 to 2026 were sorted into NAICS sectors by a fine-tuned multilingual embedding model using name, description, topics, and README, from random samples per year. [...]

Interoperability. Counts public repositories created each year whose name, description, topics, or README mention interoperability or reverse engineering, or related terms, such as clean room implementation, drop-in replacement, or protocol re-implementation.

Tags: github, ai, generative-ai, llms, coding-agents, disclosures, agentic-engineering
items.body_ko:
GitHub Octoverse 2026

저는 오늘 GitHub Universe에 와 있습니다(GitHub이 'GitHub Stars' 프로그램을 통해 무료 티켓을 제공했습니다). EVP Jay Parikh는 방금 올해의 Octoverse 보고서를 발표했으며, 특히 다음 수치를 강조했습니다:

이는 agentic engineering이 GitHub에 미치는 영향을 매우 극명하게 보여주는 것입니다. 2026년에는 병합된 pull request가 1년도 채 안 되어 월 2억 2천만 건으로 세 배 증가했습니다. 커밋은 월 73억 8천만 건으로 세 배 이상 증가했으며, 그 증가분의 대부분은 올해 하반기에 발생했습니다. 신규 리포지토리 생성률은 올해 두 배 증가하여 월 3천 3십만 건에 달했습니다.

보고서에는 산업별 새로운 수치가 포함되어 있으며, '상호 운용성 또는 리버스 엔지니어링'과 관련된 리포지토리에 대한 수치가 따로 분류되어 있습니다. 방법론 섹션에는 이를 수행한 방법에 대한 설명이 포함되어 있습니다:

공개 리포지토리 푸시 상위 국가 (프로필 위치로 조정). 각 국가의 푸시가 Octoverse 연도에 걸쳐 합산되었습니다. VPN 사용으로 인한 편향을 조정하기 위해, 이 기간 동안 푸시에 기여한 GitHub 사용자의 프로필에서 ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 코드를 추출하기 위해 LLM 분류가 사용되었습니다 [...]

산업. 2022년부터 2026년까지 생성된 공개 리포지토리는 이름, 설명, 토픽 및 README를 사용하여 미세 조정된 다국어 임베딩 모델에 의해 NAICS 섹터로 분류되었습니다. 연도별 무작위 샘플을 사용했습니다. [...]

상호 운용성. 매년 생성된 공개 리포지토리 중 이름, 설명, 토픽 또는 README에 상호 운용성 또는 리버스 엔지니어링 또는 관련 용어(예: clean room implementation, drop-in replacement 또는 protocol re-implementation)가 언급된 리포지토리의 수를 집계합니다.

items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
items.body:
I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games.

Tree Appreciator

Emberwick

Battle Drones

Pumpkin Farmer, aka Quarter Sun Cove

Four times as insulting

What happens if someone actually puts the work in?

You should build a game!

Claude Opus 5.5 in particular exhibits meaningful improvements in several areas needed to build a compelling game:

3D modeling

Music generation (see Scrimshaw Jukebox)

Game design (!)

That last one is particularly important. Models have been able to create something that looks like a game for quite a while now, as seen in my previous experiments. The challenge has been getting to a game that's actually fun to play.

Game design is a deep subject area. I won't pretend to be well versed in it - I know enough to have respect for it as a craft. Creating a novel, compelling gameplay loop which challenges players at the right level and provides a satisfying learning curve is a fine art. I didn't think the models could do it.

Then I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 to "Make it a LOT more fun"... and it did.

In the past few weeks I've vibe coded (in the classic sense of the term - no looking at the code at all) four games that I've genuinely enjoyed playing.

I attended Foo Camp in Berkeley over the weekend and met several people who were having similar experiences. Building games that play well is shockingly easy now. The new challenge is coming up with concepts for games that are novel and delightful and that wouldn't exist without AI assistance.

I haven't done an exhaustive study, but my current impression is that GPT-6 Astra isn't quite there yet. It can absolutely build a game, but its sense of fun doesn't match that of Opus 5.5. I expect OpenAI will get there by the end of the year.

Here are the four game projects that have convinced me that the models are now capable of producing fun games with very little guidance. All four are built in HTML and JavaScript and run entirely in the browser.

Tree Appreciator

The smallest game I found to be genuinely delightful is Tree Appreciator. I used the regular Claude chat interface for this - it didn't even need Claude Code.

I built this on a whim while we were driving along Skyline Boulevard looking at trees. My prompt was:

Build a three js game called "Tree appreciator" - it shows you two algorithmically generated trees and the game mechanics is about appreciating the differences between them. Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful.

I've found that telling models to use three.js works really well. Claude doesn't have its own image generation model but is capable of building full-color 3D models that look and feel excellent.

This game required no iteration or follow-up prompting at all - I got the game in a single shot. It gave me back a charming little mobile-friendly spot-the-difference game. You can play that here. Here's the chat transcript that built it.

It's pleasingly relaxing. The graphics are fun, and collecting trees that you have completed in a "herbarium" provides a nice, cosy sense of accomplishment.

Emberwick

This was a more ambitious project that I again built using regular Claude chat. I started out by building an experimental prototype of an engine for a top-down fantasy RPG:

Build a demo game engine three.js which is a top down (but at an angle) RPG - the player gets to move through the world with one or two companions. Create a fantasy village setting that demonstrates walking around outside and then shows how when the player enters a building the wall between the player and the camera goes transparent so the user can see what is happening

Add some NPCs and plenty of furniture and different types of building some with an upstairs - be creative, make it look great

Here's that first version. It worked really well!

I was inspired to increase my ambitions:

Make it not so flat - the buildings are great but the landscape itself is completely flat at the moment, fix that

Add basements to two of the buildings with a tunnel system joining them below the village

Add the start of a rocky mountain on one side of the village containing a cave with a sleeping troll

Here's that version.

When that produced a good result, I decided to push it all the way:

Now turn this into an actual game - quadruple the size of the playable area, introduce fun game mechanics, add a plot that isn't too cliche, some twists, a magic system, make it really good

We're back to prompts like "make it really good" here! Asking for a plot that "isn't too cliche" seemed to work too - it's a bit cliché, but still novel enough that I enjoyed following the story.

Unlike Tree Appreciator, this took quite a bit of additional playtesting and prompting to get to a finished version. This was mainly due to gameplay problems - things like a character not being in the right place to complete a quest because a different story element had caused them to move to another location.

Here's that final game. It has a full story that takes about 15 minutes to play through.

There's even an experimental level editor if you want to drop in your own houses, furniture, and landscape features.

Once it was all working (and I'd iterated through some gameplay bugs), I played it through from start to finish and found myself emotionally affected by the ending! I'm somewhat embarrassed by this, because everything in this game - the graphics, the plot, the characters, the music, the dialog - came from the model. My creative input was pretty much just "it's a fantasy village and there's a troll asleep in a cave".

Here's the full shared Claude chat in which I built this game.

I also fed that same initial sequence of prompts through ChatGPT GPT-6 Pro. Here's the transcript and the finished game for comparison. It looks great, but I don't think it plays nearly as well.

Battle Drones

This is by far my most successful project, which I wrote about last week. It's a Command & Conquer-style Real-Time Strategy game where two robot armies (or four as of Saturday) build units, harvest scrap, and battle over territory.

This is also the project that convinced me that Opus 5.5 knows what "fun" is.

The first versions were built back in July using Claude Fable 5. It got me to a workable 2D Command & Conquer-style game, but it wasn't great to play.

I prompted Opus 5.5 to "Make it a LOT more fun" and then later to "Port this game to three.js" and the game was transformed. There's a blow-by-blow account (prompts included) in my write-up.

Today, Battle Drones has 2-4 player multiplayer (via a vibe coded WebSockets relay server), medals, replays, seven maps, a random map generator, and a set of "mutators" that add variants of the rules.

It also lets different LLMs play against each other, using a mode where the game advances five seconds and then pauses to give different models time to interpret the new game state and line up their next set of commands. Here's a replay of Claude Haiku 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Luna:

Battle Drones is a particularly good example of Opus 5.5's ability to create 3D models. This page lets you browse all of the models in the game.

I released Battle Drones under the Apache 2.0 License last Tuesday. On Wednesday Gabriel Turpin released Panache (screenshots here), a fork of Battle Drones that reimagined the game for steampunk 1900s Belle Époque France, with new models and music and an animated intro sequence. Open source at work!

Pumpkin Farmer, aka Quarter Sun Cove

I live in Half Moon Bay, California, home of the annual Half Moon Bay Art and Pumpkin Festival, which includes a giant pumpkin weigh-off competition.

I decided to try building a game that wasn't just a cheap imitati

items.title: Quoting Terk Terkowitz
items.body:
If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for.

— Terk Terkowitz, An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI

Tags: amazon, generative-ai, agentic-engineering, ai, llms
items.body_ko:

items.title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma
items.body:
Housekeeping: I’m on the road so the voiceover will be late.
Hill-climbing is easy, knowing what to hill-climb is hard. Making scores go up is expensive, but we have a much clearer playbook for it than we do for creating meaningful benchmarks at the true frontier of AI today.
Independent evaluation of language models is under-appreciated in how hard of a task it is. These groups are not just taking current models and certifying their scores, which is a technically involved task. This is their job if AI progress is slow. When AI progress is as fast as it is, the technical details of the job are the routine work part of trying to put a single number on what makes for a good AI model today. The goal is to have a single number that is representative of current models, matching vibe checks, community sentiment, and scientific analysis, while being forward looking enough so that it’s not outdated in 3 months.
Everyone building a benchmark faces a sort of paradox. You need your benchmark to reduce to one single number, so that it is easy to discuss, use in reports, and compare models, but every method of aggregating scores comes with meaningful trade-offs. The best scientists need to do this, everyone does. It’s a matter of creating aggregating metrics that you think are most fair, knowing there will always be imperfections.
With the amount of money in the AI ecosystem today, the weight of independent evaluation is even higher – you dictate the winners and losers of a trillion dollar market. You also influence some of the models themselves, steering the shape of progress. This is a lot of pressure!
My prompt for this article is Artificial Analysis’s recent update to their Intelligence Index, v5. The AA index is the most prominent independent intelligence metric for the latest frontier models, followed in a distant second by Epoch AI’s Capabilities Index (ECI). To date, all of these have been incredibly useful for the community and massively flawed!
Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. Consider becoming a subscriber.

Language models are capable of so much today, and this scope of capabilities is growing quickly. Our era of singular intelligence indices should be phased out soon, but it will take a long time.
A summary of AAv5 is below, from their blog post, where they describe it as “reflecting real-world usage today:”
Intelligence Index v5 weights:
➤ Knowledge Work (25%): AA-Briefcase (15%), AutomationBench-AA (5%), and GDP.pdf (5%)
➤ Coding (25%): FrontierCode 2.0 (15%) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (10%)
➤ Science (25%): Terminal-Bench-Science (15%) and CritPt v2 hard subset (10%)
➤ General (25%): AA-Omniscience v1.1 15% (10% accuracy, 5% non-hallucination) and HLE-Diamond (10%)

Here’s the new ranking of models:

The problem with trying to benchmark real-world usage today is that it is extremely jagged, just like the models. The most proven use-case is coding, where open models are far more competitive and likely to keep up. In knowledge work, I’m less confident in open models.
At first glance, in aggregate, this definitely looks reasonable. Still, it shows signs of strain and confusion, as any benchmark will, with GPT 6.1 Terra beating Claude Fable 5.1. Today, some benchmarks measure the absolute frontier of capabilities, playing nicely in open-ended tasks through your favorite harness, which often does take a large model. Some other benchmarks measure certain skills that will be needed of a model in repetitive agentic tasks. I get the feeling that AA is tuning their benchmark more towards the former, a general agentic collaborator, but all of these behaviors overlap.
This takes us to the plot going around that prompted me to write this, where they showed the balance of open vs. closed models on the new benchmark. This plot shows 8 closed models beating the best to-be open-weight model, Kimi K3.1 Pro (which isn’t colored blue). This benchmark is taking the opinion of trying to measure where frontier models are moving into, which grows the gap to open models. This is an okay decision to take, but over time as existing workflows of open models become key factors of the economy, it could become a benchmark that misses where the core economic engine of the industry is.

Open models’ demise from this seems greatly exaggerated, but I do think the previous index was flattering the open weight models too strongly. Consider this plot from the Kimi K3.1 Pro launch — yes, the open models are strong and useful in some cases, but the best OpenAI and Anthropic models have been a major step ahead in their flexibility and reliability.

Some of the evaluations in AAv5 that open models are most behind on are “science” evals like terminal-bench-science and CritPT v2. Open models are behind, but the value proposition was never to compete truly at the frontier. The open model economy will be about
Reducing domains with high market demand for inference to a commodity price of hardware.

Allowing ownership of intelligence, specializing it to internal data, and controlling internal agents across many companies in the economy.

Both of these take a very long time and are partially represented in benchmarks. The supply of compute is currently so low that open model providers also are raking in solid margins – when this shrinks, we will know the system is starting to work. The same goes for diffusion into enterprises, it’s not clear what the exact ceiling on it is because of the difficult ML expertise that is needed to build evaluations and do post-training today.
Share
At the next major model cycle, say in 2-3 months with GLM 6 or Kimi 3.5, I expect the leading open model labs to make substantial steps on this index, again surprising many observers. This is a cycle we have been on for years now.
I’ve written many times about how open models keep up with the frontier, and a summary is that:
The best open models do benchmax a little. The worst open models benchmax a lot (but don’t get a ton of attention anyways).

The best open models are a bit narrower in which capabilities they cover, as seen above with their gap on scientific domains. The open model labs are working to address this, but I think it could be come a strategic error to not focus.

There’s a more nuanced version of explanations of the performance gap today, where so many of the gains in training are coming from having RL environments with distributions close to the evaluations (a longer analysis on this is here). Keeping up with rapid progress across multiple domains requires a sophisticated RL stack that not all the open model labs may possess. Some may be reliant on buying data that has moderate lead times as well.
Another part of this announcement is shifting to “private benchmarks”, where the prompts are not public, as a sign that open labs are benchmaxxing. This sort of analysis has been done before, and fits with my above theory on how open labs benchmax. It is easier to create training data to support an evaluation when you know the shape of it, but the task isn’t impossible with hidden data. All in, this is a change that directionally I think is defensible, but it’s not unanimous. For example, you’re putting complete trust in the private benchmark builder, as you no longer get the benefit of the community finding issues in the benchmark and pushing the benchmark to improve itself – which happens a lot! There is enough money on the line, where I’d rather see transparency in benchmarking and enabling many eyes to find bugs.
The final point I need to make, which does flatter the closed labs, is that the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI moved on from caring about these indices months, or even years, ago. Their focus is to a large majority on supporting internal uses – like AI R&D automation – and the use-cases of customers who are spending billions of dollars. Yes, they have team members hill climbing on other capabilities to unlock new markets, but these behaviors are to a minority extent driven by publ

items.summary_ko: Artificial Analysis v5가 출시되었지만, 벤치마킹의 어려움과 딜레마를 지적합니다. 단순한 점수 올리기는 쉽지만, AI 기술의 진정한 최전선에서 의미 있는 벤치마크를 만드는 것은 어렵다는 것입니다. 독립적인 언어 모델 평가는 모델 점수를 검증하는 기술적인 작업을 넘어, 진정한 프론티어를 정의하는 데 큰 도전이 따른다는 점을 강조합니다.
